sections.label: Singapore plastics recycling rate
sections.summary: Singapore's current plastics recycling rate is 5%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Singapore’s current plastics recycling rate is a dismal 5%.

sections.label: Global and Singapore plastics production
sections.summary: Global plastics production rose from 234 million tonnes in 2000 to 435 million tonnes in 2020, with Singapore producing 957,000 tonnes of plastic waste last year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Global plastics production jumped from 234 million tonnes in year 2000 to 435 million tonnes in year 2020 and is expected to jump by another 70% by year 2040.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Last year, in Singapore alone, we produced 957,000 tonnes of plastic waste and about four in 10 items are single-use plastics.

sections.label: Residents save on refills
sections.summary: Residents save money as the average cost of $3 per litre is about 20% to 30% cheaper than individually packed ones.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Residents save money too as the average cost of $3 per litre is about 20% to 30% cheaper than individually packed ones.

sections.label: Prevention and Reuse pillar proposal
sections.summary: The speaker recommends a Prevention & Reuse pillar with budget lines and asks NEA to consider re-use grant schemes, noting 84 paper SGRecycle bins were removed.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: I recommend an explicit "Prevention & Reuse" pillar with budget lines for pilot siting, rental offsets, measurement, reporting and verification, as well as community engagement.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: I ask NEA to consider grant schemes to incentivise re-use solutions, on top of its current emphasis on recycle and waste management.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Recently, it was reported that 84 paper SGRecycle bins were removed due to lack of sponsors.

sections.label: BYO cup savings
sections.summary: Starbucks and Toast Box customers who bring their own cups save 60 cents and 10 cents respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: For instance, customers of Starbucks and Toast Box, who bring their own cups, will enjoy savings of 60 cents and 10 cents respectively for their beverages.

sections.label: Beverage Containers Return Scheme
sections.summary: From 1 April 2026, NEA will roll out the Beverage Containers Return Scheme, returning 10 cents per plastic or metal container.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: From 1 April 2026, NEA will roll out the Beverage Containers Return Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This is a good scheme to incentivise recycling and reduce waste, by returning 10 cents for each plastic or metal container returned to the reverse vending machines.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: More importantly, I hope the Beverage Containers Return Scheme will boost our dismal plastics recycling rate.

sections.label: Plastic waste and low recycling
sections.summary: In 2024, plastics were almost 14% of waste generated, largely packaging and single-use plastics, with only 5% recycled.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In 2024, almost 14% of all waste generated was plastics, with a large proportion being packaging and single-use plastics.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Recycling of plastics is also low, with only 5% recycled in 2024.

sections.label: Disposable Carrier Bag Charge results
sections.summary: The 2023 Disposable Carrier Bag Charge encourages reusable bags; a survey found over 90% of shoppers brought their own.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: To encourage sustainable individual consumption patterns, we introduced the Disposable Carrier Bag Charge in 2023, to encourage shoppers to bring their own reusable bags when grocery shopping at supermarkets and hence reduce the use of disposables.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: A survey by NEA a year after its implementation found that more than 90% of shoppers brought their own reusable bags, with supermarket operators reporting a 70% to 80% reduction in the number of disposable carrier bags issued.

sections.label: PPP membership and platform
sections.summary: The PPP today has over 570 members and is an important platform for industry collaboration on sustainable packaging.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The PPP today has over 570 members and is an important platform for industry collaboration on sustainable packaging.

sections.label: Waste less campaign partners
sections.summary: This year 99 new partners joined NEA's Say YES to Waste Less campaign, with some offering reusable incentives.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: At a national level, we have seen many like-minded organisations come forward to offer such incentives.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This year, we welcomed 99 new partners to NEA’s annual “Say YES to Waste Less” campaign, with several such as NUS and AtTea leading the way in introducing incentives for customers to bring their own reusable tumblers or lunchboxes for takeaway food and drinks.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We welcome more to join these efforts, including coffee shops who offer discounts on drinks when patrons bring their own reusables.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Food and beverage (F&B) operators who are interested in additional recognition for their sustainable practices can also apply for the Singapore Environment Council’s Eco F&B certification.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Like other initiatives to encourage reduction and reuse, this scheme will require support from the public to deliberately collect and return your beverage containers for recycling.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: While the Government has a significant role to play in supporting this journey, sustained change will be dependent on our choices.
